title: fix(rest,objectql): the import dry run asks the engine for its verdict instead of predicting it (#4633)
body:
Fixes #4633

The import dry run promises to report the verdict the real write produces. It used to keep that promise with a hand-copied mirror of a slice of the engine's rules — `import-coerce.ts`'s `firstMissingRequiredField` and `firstConstraintViolation`. A copy cannot structurally keep up with the family it mirrors, and the gap was measured: a CSV cell aimed at a `Field.address` reported `{ ok: 1, created: 1 }` on the dry run and `{ errors: 1, code: "VALIDATION_FAILED" }` from the very same endpoint on the real write. `coerceFieldValue` routes structured value shapes through its pass-through catch-all, so no verdict was formed at all.

Ruling D (maintainer, 2026-08-06) retires the mirror rather than growing it: the dry run now asks `DataProtocol.validateData` (#6037 / PR #6474) for the verdict. The engine runs the same `validateRecord` / `evaluateValidationRules` that `insert()` runs, under this deployment's own ADR-0104 posture — so agreement is guaranteed by construction rather than by a copy kept in step by hand.

## An upstream gap: `engine.validate()` skipped two of the write path's steps

Reading what #6474 actually shipped before sizing this card (as the dispatch asked) surfaced one gap, fixed here in the same change:

`insert()` runs `applyFieldDefaults` + `initializeSummaryFields` and **then** `validateRecord`; `engine.validate()` went straight to `validateRecord`. So a required column carrying a `defaultValue`, left unmapped, was previewed `failed` and written `created` — a false alarm, the failure mode this ruling exists to prevent, pointing the opposite way from the issue's false all-clear. Both helpers are pure and synchronous (they read the registry, copy the row, and touch neither driver nor hook), so running them keeps the "nothing is written, nothing is executed" contract intact. `update` mode still does not default (#2706: an explicit `null` in a PATCH means "clear it").

This half stays in this PR rather than becoming a separate card: #6474's own commit message is headed `#4633 ruling D`, the two are halves of one work item, and this card cannot land while the upstream does not hold up its end.

## One vocabulary for the row report: the engine's field-level verdict, on both halves

`toFailedResult` now builds the row report from the engine's `ValidationError.fields[]`. Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one:

1. It names the offending **column**, which is what an import UI highlights. Before, the row carried a bare `VALIDATION_FAILED` and no `field`.
2. It is the same shape the dry run now reports, so the two halves agree on `field` and `code`, not merely on "this row failed". **Before, a `min: 0` violation was `min_value` on the dry run and `VALIDATION_FAILED` on the write** — an agreement gap hidden inside a report that looked right.

So `code` speaks one vocabulary across the whole row report: the field-level catalog (ADR-0114) that `coerceRow`'s per-cell failures already used.

Dry-run rows may additionally carry `warnings[]` — findings this deployment admits rather than rejects (ADR-0104 warn-first). The row is `ok`, because the write really would store it, but "accepted for now" becomes visible instead of living only in a server log line.

## A protocol without `validateData` is not handed a substitute

plugin-auth's identity import creates users through better-auth; its write is not the engine's write. An engine-derived preview would report findings that write never produces — a false alarm dressed as coverage. Such a dry run therefore reports coercion plus create/update/skip resolution only. `ImportProtocolLike.validateData` is a capability gate, not a lenient fallback.

## Tests

New `packages/rest/src/import-dryrun-parity.test.ts` — 14 cases against a real engine, real protocol and a real sqlite `:memory:` driver. **Every case runs the same payload twice (dry run, then for real) and asserts the two agree.** The contract is agreement, so a case that pinned only the dry run's output could not fail when the two drift apart again — which is the whole defect.

- The issue's own repro: under the strict posture both halves refuse with `field: 'billing_address'`, `code: 'invalid_type'`, `Billing Address has an invalid address value: ...`.
- **Both postures are covered**, which is the heart of the vetoed option B: on a warn-first deployment the write ACCEPTS the row, so the dry run must report `created`, not `failed`, and record the admission as a warning.
- The retired mirror's verdicts are each re-asserted through the new route: `required`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `min_length`, `max_length`, required-with-a-default satisfied unmapped, boundary values legal, and update mode judging only the supplied keys.

The eight `firstConstraintViolation` unit cases in `import-coerce.test.ts` retire with the function. Six have successors in the parity file above. Two deliberately do not: "skips system / readonly columns" and "bound-checks only the types the engine bound-checks" existed because a hand-maintained copy could disagree with the engine about which fields and types are in scope. With no copy there is no second opinion to police — that question belongs to `record-validator.ts` alone and is pinned in objectql's own tests.

## Reverse verification (direction: red, as predicted)

Deleting the newly added defaults/summary-seeding step from `engine.validate()` and re-running:

```
validate-only.test.ts         Tests   2 failed | 12 passed (14)
import-dryrun-parity.test.ts  Tests  12 failed |  2 passed (14)
```

Running the parity file before any implementation (the premise check) went red in the direction the issue describes: dry run `created: 1 / errors: 0`, real write `errors: 1`. The premise still holds on `origin/main`.

## Verification

- `packages/rest` — 65 files, 890 tests green
- `packages/objectql` — 146 files, 2452 tests green
- `packages/metadata-protocol` — 55 files, 563 tests green; `plugin-auth` — 39 files, 972 tests green (it consumes `runImport`)
- `pnpm lint` plus every `check:*` step enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, one by one — all green, including `check:type-check-debt` (`@objectstack/rest` TEST_DEBT re-measured at 146 against a recorded 163, no rise)
